title: The `EMMA` User's Guide - Enrichment Method MAtters
text: Functional Enrichment Analysis (FEA) key downstream step omics workflows, commonly applied differential expression analysis support biological interpretation generate pathway-level hypotheses. wide range tools methods available, mainly -Representation Analysis (ORA) (Khatri et al. 2012) Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) (Subramanian et al. 2005), leading substantial heterogeneity analytical choices reported results. Despite widespread use, FEA often insufficiently documented (Wijesooriya et al. 2022). Critical parameters background gene sets multiple testing correction methods frequently missing inconsistently reported scientific papers, limiting reproducibility interpretability. Currently, standardized framework exists ensure transparent reproducible documentation FEA workflows, comparable MIAME guidelines (Brazma et al. 2001). Similar approaches developed outside Bioconductor ecosystem improve transparency reproducibility analytical contexts. example, tidylog records operations performed dplyr tidyr, omicslog tracks transformations applied omics-oriented objects. However, tool specifically addresses metadata provenance requirements FEA workflows. address gap, introduce EMMA (standing Enrichment Methods MAtters), framework automatically captures key analytical parameters provenance information execution FEA methods. vignette demonstrates EMMA integrates existing tools (e.g. clusterProfiler, topGO, Enrichr, gprofiler2) execute enrichment analyses systematically capturing analysis parameters provenance information runtime, returning enrichment results without altering original format, alongside structured reusable metadata.

text: , load macrophage data perform Differential Expression Analysis DESeq2
code: # load data data(gse, package = "macrophage") # set up design dds_macrophage <- DESeqDataSet(gse, design = ~ line + condition) # preprocess rownames(dds_macrophage) <- substr(rownames(dds_macrophage), 1, 15) keep <- rowSums(counts(dds_macrophage) >= 10) >= 6 dds_macrophage <- dds_macrophage[keep, ]  # set seed for reproducibility set.seed(2711) # sample randomly for 2k genes selected_genes <- sample(rownames(dds_macrophage), 2000)  dds_macrophage <- dds_macrophage[selected_genes, ]  # run DESeq dds_macrophage <- DESeq(dds_macrophage)  # get de res for 1st contrast IFNg_vs_naive <- results(dds_macrophage,                          contrast = c("condition", "IFNg", "naive"),                          lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05) IFNg_vs_naive <- lfcShrink(dds_macrophage, coef = "condition_IFNg_vs_naive",                            res = IFNg_vs_naive,                            type = "apeglm") IFNg_vs_naive$SYMBOL <- rowData(dds_macrophage)$SYMBOL  # get de res for 2st contrast SL1344_vs_naive <- results(dds_macrophage,                          contrast = c("condition", "SL1344", "naive"),                          lfcThreshold = 1, alpha = 0.05) SL1344_vs_naive <- lfcShrink(dds_macrophage, coef = "condition_SL1344_vs_naive",                            res = SL1344_vs_naive,                            type = "apeglm") SL1344_vs_naive$SYMBOL <- rowData(dds_macrophage)$SYMBOL  # sort by adjusted p value de_list <- list(   IFNg_vs_naive = IFNg_vs_naive,   SL1344_vs_naive = SL1344_vs_naive )  de_list <- lapply(de_list, function(df) {   df <- df[order(df$padj), ]   df <- df[!is.na(df$padj) & df$padj <= 0.05, ]   df }) # set background gene list gene_universe <- rownames(dds_macrophage)
